hunt.justification: NeedyMantis is a specialized framework for long-term persistence used in targeted operations. Detecting the sideloading and C2 early is the only way to prevent follow-on modular functionality and data theft.

meta.name: NeedyMantis Modular Sideloading and WebSocket C2

related.reason: This hunt focuses on the initial deployment and C2; parsing the custom archive format and shellcode loading is handled in the deeper forensic sequel.

meta.analysis: A single rule for WinSparkle.dll or libcurl.dll creates noise when these apps are legitimately updated. This hunt correlates the unusual placement (ProgramData), the execution context (sideloading into a legitimate app), and the external network signal to achieve high-fidelity detection that a rule cannot provide.

coverage.reason: Not examined by this hunt; belongs to a separate hunt.

stages.name: Encrypted archive extraction and modular loading

scenario.summary: China-linked threat actors use the modular NeedyMantis framework for post-compromise persistence in targeted sectors. The malware is deployed via lateral movement tools like Impacket and leverages DLL sideloading in common applications like Poedit and Vim to load encrypted archives containing C2 and modular components.

meta.rationale: Start the hunt by examining workstations that run Poedit, Vim, or curl, particularly in developer and administrative groups.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has established long-term access by sideloading modular components into legitimate processes like Poedit or Vim, using encrypted archives staged in unusual directories to bypass detection.

references.name: MSRC Blog — NeedyMantis: Unpacking a post-compromise malware family

blind_spots.risk: Without protocol awareness, persistent 443 traffic might be dismissed as standard encrypted browser traffic or update checks.
blind_spots.question: Whether the persistent TCP traffic is an authenticated WebSocket stream
blind_spots.requires: Deep packet inspection with WebSocket protocol parsing
blind_spots.remediation: Enable WebSocket protocol logging on the perimeter proxy or firewall.

blind_spots.risk: The framework stages its second and third components inside an encrypted archive that hb_file_activity cannot see inside.
blind_spots.question: What files are contained within the staged extensionless archives
blind_spots.requires: Decompression and decryption capability on the host
blind_spots.remediation: Implement sandbox detonation for extensionless archives found in ProgramData.

hunt.name: NeedyMantis Modular Sideloading and WebSocket C2
hunt.description: NeedyMantis is a modular framework observed in targeted operations against government and telecommunications sectors. It relies on DLL sideloading within common software and maintains a persistent WebSocket-based connection for command and control. This hunt identifies the framework by tracing the initial file deployment via Impacket-style patterns, confirming the execution through rare module loads from non-standard paths, and identifying the low-prevalence DNS resolution of known C2 infrastructure.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, file_path, file_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (activity_id = 1 OR activity_id = 3) AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\programdata\\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\users\\public\\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\program files\\poedit\\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\program files\\vim\\%') AND instr(',' || '{{target_dlls}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(file_name) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify the initial placement of the sideloading DLLs and accompanying archives in ProgramData or Program Files subfolders, mimicking the lateral movement observed in the report.
config.expected_signal: A row showing a DLL like WinSparkle.dll or libcurl.dll being written to ProgramData. Silence indicates no obvious staging of these components was captured.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, module_name, module_path, time FROM hb_module_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{target_dlls}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(module_name) || ',') > 0 AND (LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\\programdata\\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\\users\\public\\%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Confirm that the target processes (Poedit, curl, etc.) are actually loading the masquerading DLLs from unusual paths.
config.expected_signal: A legitimate process loading a DLL from a path where it does not normally reside. This is the core behavioral indicator of NeedyMantis.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(module_name) as name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count FROM hb_module_activity WHERE (LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\\programdata\\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\\users\\public\\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Stack-count the identified modules to ensure the signal is not fleet-wide noise from a standard administrative tool.
config.expected_signal: A low host count for the specific module names identifies the targeted nature of the payload.
